page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-8GB is an entry-tier virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 8.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core), 40 GB of local SSD storage, and no GPU hardware. The processor provides 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1 data cache, with support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and hardware cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). One complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded throughput balanced against shared multi-core limits. The instance reaches top-tier single-core stress-ng performance (3877.27) and high compression capability, logging 41.73 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 17.93 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics reflect the two-core allocation, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3225.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 36.3 GB/sec, placing it in the lower quartile. Memory throughput is consistent with mid-range tiers, registering 49.65 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 46.59 GB/sec for writes.

Application and synthetic task testing reflects a general-purpose profile. Static web serving throughput reaches 9.71 GB/sec within the middle tier, while Redis SET operations sustain 5.88 million operations per second. Smaller local machine learning workloads show capable performance, recording 769.99 prompt tokens per second and 185.93 generation tokens per second on a 135M parameter LLM, but drop substantially on larger 7B models (7.27 generation tokens per second).

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM configuration and shared CPU model, this server delivers practical cost efficiency for lightweight production and development environments. The primary tradeoff lies in raw multi-core scaling and shared CPU allocation, making it less suitable for high-concurrency compilation, large-scale data science, or demanding databases. It is best aligned with lightweight web serving, microservices, staging environments, utility automation, and small-scale caching layers.
description: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-8GB is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, it provides 2 shared vCPUs, 8.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), and 40 GB of local SSD storage, without GPU hardware. Benchmark metrics show high single-core compute and data compression throughput, placing in the upper tier for single-threaded stress-ng (3877.27) and single-threaded gzip compression (41.73 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded scores and complex operations such as PassMark database tests reflect the constraints of its two-core footprint. The instance maintains stable memory bandwidth alongside 9.71 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Featuring a 1:4 CPU-to-RAM ratio, the STARTER-2xCPU-8GB offers balanced resource allocation suited for small web services, microservice APIs, staging systems, and background processing tasks.
